_doc: CPU-binding experiment (task: do exclusive pinned cores help now that wal is no longer fsync-bound at 270k+ ops/s?). Own cluster bench-cpubind created with STATIC_CPU=1 (kubelet cpuManagerPolicy=static on the server pool) and deployed with GUARANTEED=1 (gke/durable-streams-splitlane-guaranteed.yaml: every container requests==limits, server cpu integer 8 -> EXCLUSIVE pinned cores). Same split-lane layout + image (:ckptoff) + args as wal-splitlane's ref-3s, so the control is wal-splitlane ref-3s = 286k @10k / 272k @100k on shared cores. Success = bound arm meaningfully above 286k/272k (>= +5%); parity means CPU binding is not a lever at this throughput and the task closes. VERIFY at deploy: kubectl exec ... cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.effective in the server container should show a dedicated core set, not all cores. Requires STATIC_CPU=1 SPLITLANE=1 GUARANTEED=1 SERVER_LOCAL_SSD_BLOCK=1 SPOT_SERVER=1 IMG_SERVER=...:ckptoff.
